chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man entered upon Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) and said, 'Your wife, the Shaybaniyyah, is outspoken and curses Ali (peace be upon him). If it pleases you that I let you hear it from her, I will let you hear it.' He said, 'Yes.' He said, 'So when tomorrow comes, at the time you intend to go out as you usually do, return and hide in the side of the house.' He said, 'So when it was the next day, he hid in the side of the house, and the man came and spoke to her, and that became clear from her, so he let her go her way, and she was pleasing to him.'

key_terms.اَلشَّيْبَانِيَّةَ: The Shaybaniyyah (a title/name for the wife of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn)
key_terms.خَارِجِيَّةٌ: Outspoken / Eloquent / One who speaks freely
key_terms.فَخَلَّى سَبِيلَهَا: So he let her go her way / He allowed her to remain

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn's wife, the Shaybaniyyah, and her cursing of Imam Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates the practical application of the principle that a spouse's character does not invalidate the marriage contract (*nikah*), distinguishing between lineage-based prohibitions and behavioral ones. Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) demonstrates patience and discretion by privately verifying the wife's habit of cursing him rather than reacting publicly, thereby preserving domestic harmony. This narrative underscores the Shia scholarly view that minor faults or even disrespect towards the Imam himself do not necessitate divorce if the spouse remains agreeable to the husband.
